messages:
sam: Thanks for coming to today’s all-hands — starting this thread for the leftover strategy questions folks raised. Short answers + follow-ups below.

jordan: Quick ask — can someone give a one-liner we can use in partner decks that explains our mission without sounding like every other AI vendor?

sam: Our short line: 'Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible to every engineering team.' Use that as the default. If partner needs more: two-sentence explainer = 'We provide a unified inference runtime across hosted, reserved, and private deployments so teams get predictable latency, cost, and controls without building the stack. The result: faster time-to-market and stable unit economics for production LLM features.'

elaine: Follow-up: how do we position vs the big cloud AI endpoints (fastest-to-integrate) and vs API-first LLM providers (model breadth)? Sales keeps asking what to emphasize.

sam: TL;DR: emphasize predictable economics and ops controls. Cloud incumbents = great for general-purpose workloads but they often leave customers operating variance on latency/cost and integration differences across regions. API-first LLM providers = easy access, but absent production-grade routing, batching, and fallback policies you pay more at scale or see regressions.

ravi: From eng perspective — customers care about three things: 1) latency SLOs, 2) cost per request, 3) support for private deployments. Anything else we should bake into messaging?

sam: Add 'reliability under load' and 'transparent performance profiles' — call out that our model catalog includes verified perf numbers and that we offer automatic fallbacks (model variants/regions) to keep apps online.

maya: Sales wants the top 3 competitive objections + suggested responses so they can prep rebuttals.

elaine: Objection 1: 'Why not just use Cloud X managed endpoints?' Response: 'Clouds are great for prototyping. For production with strict latency/cost goals, we provide workload-aware batching, prefix/KV caching, and optimized kernels that reduce per-token cost while keeping latency bounded.'

elaine: Objection 2: 'Why not a cheaper open-source self-hosted stack?' Response: 'Self-hosting trades capital and ops effort for control. We offer the same low-level optimizations plus orchestration, observability, SLAs, and rollout tooling so you can focus on product not infra.'

elaine: Objection 3: 'We need on-prem for compliance — can you support it?' Response: 'Yes — Redwood Private offers a VPC/on‑prem option with customer-managed control plane, KMS integrations, and audit logs. We have a clear path and support plan for regulated deployments.'

jordan: Nice. Any concrete asks for the product/marketing teams to make these responses easy for reps?

sam: Action items: 1) Product to produce a 1-page 'Why Redwood' (one-liner + three differentiators + top metrics) — @elaine please own. 2) GTM to add a slide comparing typical cost/latency tradeoffs vs clouds + self-hosted — @maya to own. 3) Sales ops to get standard rebuttal bullets into the playbook and share test prompts for evals — @jordan please coordinate.

elaine: Will do. ETA for 1-pager: EOD next Tues. I’ll include a short perf table (latency median/p90, cost per 1k tokens) and a short customer example.

ravi: Quick tech note for follow-up: we should include typical batching configs and a short note on fallback policy (how models are chosen under capacity pressure). I’ll draft a 2-paragraph doc and share in #docs.

maya: Sales will want customer-facing case studies. Can we get a short list of 2–3 reference customers that are ok with basic metrics?

sam: Yes — Ops & CS will coordinate outreach. @ravi @elaine — please share candidate customers by end of week.

ops-bot: Deploy notifier: production inference runtime v2.3.1 rolled to hosted region us-west-2 — no known impact.

sam: Thanks all. If anyone has follow-ups that need leadership input, drop them here and I’ll escalate. Otherwise I’ll check back after the one-pager lands and we’ll run a short sync with sales next week. :thumbsup:
